title: Agent Council
markdown:
The Executive (`openexecutive.orchestrator.executive.Executive`) is a single coherent persona that fans out to specialist sub-agents via Anthropic tool use. Each specialist subclasses `openexecutive.agents.base.BaseAgent`, carrying a `name`, `domain`, and `model`, and exposes `analyze(...)`, which wraps the question in user-turn context and calls Claude through the per-call provider. That context is per call and never cached: `<company_stage>` (the stage from the company profile — specialists never see the profile itself), in solo mode `<principal_role>` (what kind of principal the advice is for, in plain words, with their title and remit — `router.principal_role_context`), `<department_memory>`, `<past_decisions>`, `<failure_cases>`, `<relevant_knowledge>` and `<conversation_context>`, outermost first. The specialist's own system prompt is a static domain constant under one `cache_control` block, so it stays byte-identical across companies and profile edits. A chat turn takes the stage from its session's profile (the one the Executive reasons over, and the one an eval scenario injects); workflow steps and the MCP server's `consult_specialist` read it fresh from the profile on disk. The role tag follows the turn's mode: a chat turn pins the role on its session with the mode (`pin_turn_principal_role`: the session's `principal_role` override, else the workspace settings) and sends it in solo and nothing in team, so the org block, every specialist in the turn and any workflow the turn starts see the same role; callers with no chat turn read it fresh (`load_principal_role`: the current session's mode and role, else the workspace's), and a failed read sends no tag rather than failing the consult. The CFO, CSO and sales prompts key their advice on it: for a bootstrapped, self-funded or solo company they drop venture fundraising benchmarks and work from cash, and raise only if the founder wants to.

Routing uses one `consult_specialist` tool. Beside it the Executive carries its skill tools (`search_skills`, `load_skill`, `create_skill`, `update_skill`, `delete_skill` — shown to users as **playbooks**; `create_skill` / `update_skill` / `delete_skill` never change the library — they save a draft (`knowledge/skill_drafts.py`) that a person approves on the Playbooks tab, and the reply links to it; `update_skill` / `delete_skill` (and `create_skill`, for a name a workflow still follows) refuse any built-in name (including a company's customized copy) and any company playbook a workflow (even a switched-off custom one) follows — workflows read playbooks at run time, approved scheduled ones included, and this loop also runs on inbound email and chat, so only a person on the Playbooks tab can change what a workflow follows; a hidden built-in is invisible to search and load; each `search_skills` hit lists the `workflows` that follow it, and the persona routes "the finished deliverable" to that workflow and quick or partial asks to the playbook inline); Tool calls made while proactive work is tagged (scheduler dispatch, reflection, research, alert review) feed the Attunement outcome ledger. Goals have three tools: `list_department_goals`, `update_department_goal` (progress the user reports) and `create_goal` (a new goal the principal states, filed under an area by slug or title and creating the area when none matches — see Org). `create_goal` runs only for the principal on a verified surface, and no unattended run is offered it: the tools in `schedule_tools.UNATTENDED_WITHHELD_TOOLS` are dropped from reflection's and research's toolkits by `unattended_toolkit`, and from the chat loop when its Session is marked `unattended` — the scheduler's PROACTIVE TRIGGER run, whose prompt quotes stored intent text; a call the model emits anyway gets an error tool_result. `record_decision_outcome` records how a past decision turned out — the weekly review lists decisions older than 30 days with no outcome as `[decision N]` — writing `decisions.outcome` (`episodic.update_decision`) and auditing the rationale; it has `create_goal`'s gate (the principal on a verified surface only; everyone else gets an audited refusal) and is in `UNATTENDED_WITHHELD_TOOLS` too. A missing or unknown id returns the decisions still waiting on an outcome, so the model can retry with the right one. Its schema is static; the solo persona has one line on it, and team mode learns it from the tool description, so the team persona is byte-identical. Attunement adds `list_open_loops` (what a person owes — everyone's for the principal only in a private conversation, otherwise the caller's own) and `close_open_loop`, which only closes a loop when the turn's resolved speaker is the principal or the loop's owner — an unrostered sender, a signed-in web user not on the roster, and unattended sessions are refused. The roster write tools (`upsert_person`, `archive_person`, `set_department_head`) are the principal's alone, and only on a surface that verified the speaker — the web chat, the principal's own Slack or Discord, or a private Telegram chat when `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set to a value Telegram can send (Telegram identifies the chat rather than the sender, and without that secret its webhook accepts anyone's update). A teammate, an email (even from the principal's address), Google Chat, the CLI, the MCP server and unattended runs get `status: refused` (audited, and no action chip), because a team member's People row is also the web sign-in and outbound-email allow-list. `upsert_person` takes `kind` (`team` / `contact`; a new person defaults to `contact` in solo mode, an update keeps the current kind) and `list_people` returns both kinds with `kind` — contacts only on the principal's own verified turn (they are private to the principal; anyone else gets the team as if no contact existed) — while `lookup_person` searches the team only. The same verified-principal rule, as `people_tools.contacts_reachable_now()`, decides whether a turn may reach a **contact** at all: `message_person`, the raw DM tools, `create_calendar_event` / `create_instant_meeting` attendees and the MCP gateway's Gmail / Calendar / Drive gates treat a contact exactly like an unknown person on every other turn, so no refusal reveals that one exists. A turn about the principal's private mail (`Session.private_to_principal`) reaches the principal only. It is neither offered nor allowed to run `schedule_tools.PRIVATE_TURN_WITHHELD_TOOLS` — everything that reaches someone else, publishes where the team reads, or starts work outside the turn: the broadcasts, meeting bookings and cancellations, `run_workflow` and research, follow-ups and workflow nudges, watches, artifacts, goal updates, saved workflows, skill drafts, and `load_mcp_server` (it connects to any URL, which can carry the turn's content). Through `search_tools` and `call_tool` it reaches only `schedule_tools.PRIVATE_TURN_MCP_TOOLS`: Google Workspace reads and the Gmail send and draft the gateway narrows to the principal. A search shows it nothing else, and a call to anything else (Google Chat, a Docs or Drive write, `manage_event`, another server) is refused (`schedule_tools.private_turn_withholds`). A call the model emits anyway, MCP tools included, gets an error tool_result and writes an audit row, and every audit row the turn writes is the principal's alone. Multiple parallel `tool_use` blocks in a single assistant turn fan out concurrently through `router.route_parallel`, each running its own domain-filtered ChromaDB query before the specialist sees the question. The fan-out is failure-isolated per call: a specialist that raises or returns no text becomes an `UNAVAILABLE` tool_result (`router.specialist_unavailable_result`) instead of failing the whole turn, and its area — "finance", "legal", never the specialist's name — is reported to the user under the web reply, or by the Executive in its reply on other channels, unless another call to it answered that turn. A failed specialist does not count as consulted, so it takes no committee seat. Cancellation (Stop) still propagates. The Executive then synthesizes the returned analyses into one reply.

The ten entries in `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY` (`openexecutive.orchestrator.router`):

| Key | Agent | Domain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cso` | `StrategyAgent` | strategy |
| `cfo` | `FinanceAgent` | finance |
| `chro` | `HRAgent` | hr |
| `gc` | `LegalAgent` | legal |
| `coo` | `OperationsAgent` | operations |
| `cmo` | `MarketingAgent` | marketing |
| `cpo` | `ProductAgent` | product |
| `sales` | `SalesAgent` | sales |
| `board_comms` | `BoardCommsAgent` | board |
| `triage` | `TriageAgent` | triage |

Models: specialists default to `claude-sonnet-5`; a deep-reasoning tier uses `claude-opus-5` (adaptive thinking); routing/fast classification uses `claude-haiku-4-5`. The Council's **Deep reasoning** toggle is honoured on Claude Opus/Sonnet (direct or via OpenRouter) and on any OpenRouter model whose live catalog entry supports `reasoning` (today all OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and Grok entries; not Llama) — the request translator turns Anthropic adaptive thinking + effort into OpenRouter's `reasoning` parameter. It is a silent no-op on models that can't reason, and disabled for Haiku, which rejects adaptive thinking. The Council picks a model in two steps: a **Provider** dropdown (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, xAI, Local, …), then a **Model** dropdown limited to that provider, with readable names ("Claude Opus 5.5") and the raw id and serving route shown underneath. The Anthropic group combines the direct Claude models (`claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`) with any Claude generation that exists only on OpenRouter, and never lists a model twice. With `OPENROUTER_ENABLED`, the non-Anthropic entries come from OpenRouter's live `/models` catalog (fetched at startup, refreshed in the background, filtered to tool-capable paid text models from an allowlisted vendor set), falling back to a built-in snapshot if the fetch fails. Eight Council-only agents are model/prompt-overridable in the UI but NOT callable via `consult_specialist`, because they are deliberately kept out of `SPECIALIST_REGISTRY`: `quality_judge` (committee review), `utility_fast` (gates, titles, decision parsing), `research` (the `executive_research` fan-out), `fixture_generator` (invents demo companies), `engagement_intake` (models a real client from intake material), `onboarding_interviewer` (interviews a new user about their own company and drafts its profile, people and departments), `workflow_designer` (runs the conversational New workflow wizard on `/jobs/new`: searches the available tools, asks clarifying questions, then drafts a validated dynamic-workflow definition for the user to review), and `workflow_actor` (runs a workflow's `action` steps: a bounded tool-use loop limited to the tools the user approved for that step). `fixture_generator`, `engagement_intake` and `onboarding_interviewer` share one shape — a forced tool call producing a whole company, validated for referential integrity, with a single repair retry — but opposite epistemics: the fixture author invents, the other two extract and leave unstated facts empty rather than guessing. When the workspace is in solo mode, `onboarding_interviewer`'s first user turn is prefixed with a short hint (`interview.solo_hint(role_kind)`, one static constant per role kind from the onboarding role step): the draft names only the principal, as principal, and no departments; an owner is asked about the offer, customers, pricing, cash and runway, an in-house executive about their organisation (drafted as the company — their employer), function, remit, manager, team size as context and what they are measured on, an independent about their practice, clients and pricing, and with no role given the role-neutral `SOLO_HINT` asks which they are. The hint rides in the user turn and the tool array is unchanged, so the cached system prompt and tool prefix are the same in both modes.

One more structured-output utility agent sits beside `triage`: `openexecutive.agents.alert_review.AlertReviewAgent` (routing model, one forced `emit_alert_reviews` tool call, never raises). The alert review job hands it a batch of open alerts with evidence and gets back, per alert, a verdict (relevant / changed / resolved / stale), a confidence, the evidence it relied on, a one-line note, why-now, an optional deadline, and a recommended move (none / route / nudge / escalate / draft / suggest_workflow / merge / close) with its parameters. Like `triage`, it never mutates state — `alerts.review.apply_verdict` executes the verdicts deterministically within authority, so the model's job is judgment, not action.

**Solo mode.** When the workspace (or the turn's session) is solo — one person using Open Executive for themselves — the Executive works for that one person, the principal, whatever their role: they may run their own business, lead a function inside a larger organisation, or work independently, and the persona reads which from the context instead of assuming it — the role lines under "Your Principal" in the org block, when the principal gave their role (workspace settings: kind, title, reports to, remit, measured on). Its persona swaps the team sections ("You Are a Member of This Executive Team", "Choosing Who to Tell", "Departments & Org Coordination") for "You Work for One Person", "The People in Their World", "Who Hears From You" and "Goals and Areas". Solo means only the principal uses Open Executive — not that they have no people: their manager, direct reports, peers, clients, investors and board are contacts. The Executive helps the principal work with them (a 1:1 or review prep, an update or budget case for their manager or board, a negotiation) but does not coordinate them, contacts them only when the principal asks and only if they are a contact, and never offers to loop the principal in. Every specialist stays relevant — HR for the principal's own reports, board and investor communications for reporting upward. Goals are grouped by *area* (the tools' `department_slug` is the area's slug). The chat loop withholds `send_department_message`, `send_company_broadcast` and `set_department_head` from its tool list, and a call to one of them anyway gets a JSON error tool_result instead of running. The mode is resolved once per turn and pinned on the session, so the persona, the org block, the tools and every tool handler agree — a switch made mid-turn applies from the next turn. Team mode is unchanged.

Every specialist *advises* — each returns domain analysis the Executive synthesizes into one voice. None of them act on the company's behalf; the side-effecting tools in the main loop (schedule, people, departments, broadcast, watchlist, workflows) belong to the Executive, not to a specialist.

One tool writes under someone else's name, and it is fenced in code rather than the prompt. `ghostwrite_email` (**Act as me**, `orchestrator.delegation_tools`) writes an email as the person the Executive is speaking with and saves it as a draft in their own Gmail; it never sends. It lives in its own registry, never `_ALL_SKILL_TOOLS`, so reflection, research and workflow toolkits can never carry it. The chat loop adds it only on a turn `delegation.settings.pin_turn_delegation` offered it to — the principal, with it on, verified, in a conversation private to them (the web chat, a Slack or Discord DM, a verified private Telegram chat), on an attended turn — and builds that turn's handler map from both registries, so on any other turn a call to it is an unknown tool. Recipients are chosen in code, never by the model, and the text comes from the **ghostwriter** (`delegation.ghostwriter`), a tool-less call with a constant prompt plus the person's "How I write" profile. The ghostwriter is deliberately not a Council agent: the Council's edit routes have no principal check. See **Act as Me (Delegation)**.

The Executive can also launch *any* workflow conversationally: `orchestrator.workflow_run_tools` adds `list_workflows` (the launchable catalog with each workflow's inputs) and `run_workflow` (runs a built-in or custom workflow to completion and returns its artifact, checkpointing approval gates as `awaiting_human`). `run_workflow` runs the weekly review, and in solo mode the morning brief, only for the principal on a verified surface (`Workflow.principal_only_modes`, `create_goal`'s rule); anyone else gets an audited refusal that does not name the rule. This makes the `/jobs` catalog reachable from chat — see the Workflows section.

Deliverables are first-class too. `orchestrator.artifact_tools` gives the Executive three tools: `draft_artifact` publishes a memo, web page (`html`), Word document (`docx`), spreadsheet (`xlsx`, from structured `sheets`) or a `link` to something it created in one of the principal's connected apps through the generic MCP gateway (`search_tools` → `call_tool`, any server — no vendor is named), and returns the artifact's id and link; `list_artifacts` and `get_artifact` let it find and reread its own past work (drafts and workflow outputs alike, through the same `artifact_records` read model the API uses). Revising is `draft_artifact(supersedes=<id>)`, which archives the earlier version. When the principal asks for a deliverable the tool is always used; the "quiet is the right default" bar applies only to unprompted drafts. The format enum is a hard-coded sorted tuple so the cached tool schema stays byte-stable. Delivery: `message_person(person_id, text, artifact_id?)` appends the artifact's title and a `UI_BASE_URL/artifacts/<id>` link (through the same outbound guard as any DM; the link needs Open Executive access), and a Gmail send/draft can attach the file itself by `artifact_id` — see Integrations.

The Executive also backs the **Ask OE** panel's form-fill tier via `orchestrator.form_tools.propose_form_values`: when a chat turn arrives with a `<page_context>` block describing a form on the user's screen, the Executive can propose values for it. The proposal is delivered to the UI as a `form_patch` SSE event and placed into the form as highlighted suggestions — the tool never saves or submits anything; the user reviews and saves manually. The tool is **always** in the tool list (tool definitions sit at the top of the cached prompt prefix, so a conditionally-present tool would invalidate the prompt cache whenever panel and non-panel turns alternate); its description restricts usage to turns that carry a form descriptor.
